A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work on convergent f-DP analysis of Noisy-FedAvg and Noisy-FedProx. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: Section V reports original MNIST and CIFAR-10 accuracy experiments, sensitivity studies in Figure 2, and the performance comparison in Tables VI–VII.

after.justification: Section 5 retains original MNIST and CIFAR-10 accuracy results, sensitivity studies in Figure 2, and the performance comparison in Tables 6–7.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Equations (2)–(4) retain the same clipped-gradient updates, Gaussian client noise, averaging, and proximal regularization. The four learning-rate schedules are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same heterogeneous MNIST and CIFAR-10 classification tasks. Removing a client-count configuration from the accuracy table changes experimental settings, without changing dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Tables VII/7 retain Noisy-FedAvg and the same three Noisy-FedProx settings. Tables IV/4 also retain the same nine theoretical comparators; v1's Zhang et al. (2022) corresponds to v2's Zhang and Tang (2022).

E3.justification: The reported accuracy grid narrows from m = 20, 50, 100 in Table VI to m = 50, 100 in Table 6. Local intervals, noise levels, per-client sample allocations, and TK = 30000 remain unchanged. This establishes a reporting-scope revision, not a rerun.

E4.justification: The accuracy analysis of noise effects across client scales loses its m = 20 slice. Figure 2's sensitivity sweeps over m, K, V, and alpha, and Tables VII/7's proximal-regularization comparison, remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Tables VI/6 both specify five repetitions to compute mean and variance and use the same uncertainty-reporting practice. No seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or additional statistical procedures are introduced.

E6.justification: Table 6 removes 18 accuracy-and-uncertainty entries and six divergence entries for m = 20. All 36 retained accuracy-and-uncertainty pairs match exactly. Figure 2 and Tables VII/7 retain their results; the removed accuracy entries do not reappear in the appendices.

T1.justification: The assumptions, sensitivity bounds, privacy theorems, and Appendix A.1–A.3 proofs retain their mathematical substance. Table I/1 uses equivalent algebraic expressions, and Appendix A.2 shortens an intermediate learning-rate derivation without changing its stated result.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the claims of convergent privacy for non-convex FL-DP, improved privacy through proximal regularization, and conversion to other DP frameworks. Abstract and conclusion trimming does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Both retain the explanations involving data/model sensitivity and noise averaging, the optimization–privacy tradeoff in alpha, and the limitations of continuous learning-rate decay for online clients. No substantive new interpretation or applicability boundary is introduced.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures retain the same model choices, Dirichlet-0.1 partitioning, per-client sample allocations, and update specifications. Beyond the reported grid reduction, there are no separate changes to implementation instructions, resource information, or code/data access.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to composition-based privacy analyses and shifted interpolation are retained. Author–year citations and clarified attribution of existing f-DP background do not substantively change the research positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract is shortened, several explanations and the concluding empirical recap are trimmed, and section/theorem numbering and author information are revised. The appendices move before the references, while the main narrative and section sequence remain largely intact.

P2.justification: The two-column main text becomes single-column, with extensive changes to typography, spacing, and figure/table placement. Table 1 abbreviates learning-rate labels, Table 4 drops a duplicated f-DP column, and Table 6 removes the m = 20 columns. The three figures are retained and rescaled.

improvement.justification: Table 6 removes the m = 20 accuracy results while Section 5 still quotes accuracy changes for that group, weakening verification of the client-scale discussion. The roomier layout and modest editing offer presentation benefits, but the loss of directly relevant supporting entries creates a limited net decline. The core theory and remaining experiments are unchanged.
